notes:
COORD-ORDER CONTRACT (asymmetric, load-bearing): the FRONTEND sends near={lat},{lng} (LATITUDE FIRST) — matching SuggestEndpoint's leniently-parsed lat,lng contract (parts[0]=lat). WI-1's BACKEND then flips this to Mapy's preferNear={lng},{lat} (LONGITUDE FIRST) internally. Two distinct order contracts; getGeoSuggest formats `${near.lat},${near.lng}` deliberately, do NOT 'fix' it to lng-first. Dot-decimal via URLSearchParams (JS has no cs-CZ comma trap — mirrors getGeoReverse).

GPS-NULL PLACEHOLDER (deliberate, do not flag): pickSuggestLocation's precedence is map-center -> GPS -> config-center, but MapOrderPage supplies gpsLocation:null because no geolocation hook exists in the customer shell yet. The helper accepts the tier so a future GPS wire is a one-line change (per the designer's documented decision + spec Assumptions).

COARSE ROUNDING: pickSuggestLocation rounds the chosen coord to 2 decimals (~1.1 km) INSIDE the helper, deliberately coarser than client.ts roundCoord's 4 decimals (~11 m), so tiny map nudges keep the same value and the TanStack key ['geo','suggest',debounced,near] stays stable (no re-query storm). near is NOT debounced (only the text is) — a coarse-near change re-queries immediately; TanStack hashes the key by value so a fresh-but-equal near object does not refetch, which is why NO useMemo/useCallback was added (rules/web-performance.md#memoization-policy, bit UC-015 WI-4).

client.ts near type is the INLINE structural { lat; lng } | null, NOT the features/ LatLng — client.ts lives in shared/ and must not import a feature-layer type (rules/web-architecture.md#api-client). LatLng (from features/customer/shell/mapCamera, sanctioned cross-sub-feature import) is used only in suggestLocation.ts, useSuggest.ts, DestinationSearch.tsx, MapOrderPage.tsx.

MapOrderPage.test.tsx has NO QueryClientProvider (all query hooks are mocked). Because the page now calls useGeoConfig directly, the test MUST mock ../../../shared/map/useGeoConfig (done) — otherwise every test throws 'No QueryClient set'.
